data.name: Artemius
data.gender_notes: Artemius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'Artemios', meaning gift of the earth. In Christian tradition, the name Artemius is associated with Saint Artemius of Antioch, a 3rd-century martyr. The name Artemius carries the meaning “Gift of the earth” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Artemius usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizing connection to the natural world and appreciation for its beauty.
data.etymology: Artemius belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift of the earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Artemius total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Artemius
in_english.long_meaning: the name Artemius is derived from the Greek name Artemios, meaning one devoted to or protected by Artemis, the goddess of the hunt, and in Christian context, the name signifies devotion, piety, and spiritual protection

data.cultural_impact: The name Artemius has Greek origins and is associated with the goddess Artemis, the goddess of the hunt, wilderness, childbirth, and the protector of the diseased and young animals. The name carries the rich cultural heritage of Ancient Greece, which has significantly influenced Western art, literature, and philosophy.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the name Artemius symbolizes the gift of life and nature's bounty. As a tribute to Saint Artemius of Antioch, the name inspires spiritual reflection on the sanctity of life and nature. It serves as a reminder to cherish the wonders of creation and offer gratitude for the gifts of the earth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Artemius is a name of Greek origin, associated with the goddess Artemis, the goddess of wilderness, childbirth, and hunting. In Christian context, it may symbolize a connection to the natural world, protection during childbirth, or a dedication to the pursuit of spiritual growth through the disciplines of hunting or introspection.

biblical_reference.note: not directly mentioned in the Bible

historical_references.reference: Theodosius I (379-395 AD) ordered the destruction of temples dedicated to non-Christian gods, including Artemis at Ephesus. This marked the end of pagan worship in the Roman Empire.
Justinian I (527-565 AD) rebuilt the Church of the Holy Wisdom (Hagia Sophia) in Constantinople, dedicating it to the Christian Virgin Mary. Previously, the temple had been dedicated to Artemis.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Artemius has its roots in Greek mythology, where Artemis was the goddess of the hunt, wilderness, childbirth, and chastity. In the Christian context, Saint Artemius is revered as a martyr and healer, particularly in the Eastern Orthodox Church. In the modern world, the name Artemius is seen in various contexts, including the medical industry where it is used as a male name. On Reddit, there are several subreddits dedicated to Greek mythology, and discussions about Saint Artemius are common. On Wikipedia, there are extensive articles about both Greek goddess Artemis and Saint Artemius. Goodreads, a platform for readers and book reviews, has several books with the name Artemius in the title, some of which explore the mythological and religious aspects of the name.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Peter Artemius in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Artemius, which means "Gift of the earth". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
